Article Title: After made-in-India bullet train, new high-speed corridors to get indigenous signalling system
Article Text:
India will develop its own control protocols for high-speed rail.

India’s indigenous signalling system for bullet trains

7 High-Speed Rail Corridors Planned

India is aiming to achieve new milestones in manufacturing with its first bullet train project. After deciding to manufacture the high-speed train indigenously for the Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train corridor, Indian Railways is now looking at in-house advanced signalling system for other upcoming corridors.Indian Railways is developing an indigenous signalling protocol for high-speed rail called the Bharat Train Control System (BTCS). The system is being designed specifically for Indian operating conditions and aims to eliminate dependence on foreign signalling protocols for the nearly 7,000 km of new bullet train corridors planned across the country.Earlier this month, former Japanese minister Hideki Makihara criticised India for not exclusively adopting Japanese technology for the MAHSR project, pointing to its decision to use open-source signalling protocols instead of Japan's Digital Automatic Train Control system.Responding to these concerns, officials said trains supplied by Japan's Hitachi are compatible with ETCS, but added that "offers from them (Japan) need to come first".Also Read | Why India making its own bullet trains is a big deal - explained The official further said India is also "open to allowing switchover to Japanese protocols once suppliers place appropriate proposals".Officials told ET that approvals for the designs and route alignments of future high-speed rail corridors are expected to be completed by mid-2027."India will develop its own control protocols for high-speed rail," a senior official told the financial daily, adding that the new system will build on the experience gained from the Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail (MAHSR) corridor, where the European Train Control System (ETCS) is currently being deployed."The Bharat Train Control System will be open-source, cost-effective and can be tailored to requirements of rapid and safe deployment across the country," the official said, adding that once developed, the technology could also be offered to other countries.The official added that introducing an indigenous high-speed rail signalling protocol would provide a significant boost to domestic railway design companies and equipment manufacturers.In June last year, the National High Speed Rail Corporation Ltd (NHSRCL) awarded a Rs 4,100 crore contract for the signalling system on the Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail (MAHSR) corridor to a consortium comprising India's Dineshchandra R Agrawal Infracon Pvt Ltd and Germany's Siemens.The consortium is deploying an ETCS Level 2-based signalling system capable of supporting train operations at speeds of up to 350 kmph.The Delhi-Meerut Rapid Rail Corridor, which currently operates India's fastest train, is also equipped with ETCS Level 2 signalling, supplied and implemented by France's Alstom.According to industry observers, the decision to adopt ETCS Level 2 for the Japan-backed MAHSR project enabled a broader pool of equipment suppliers to participate.
Article Summary: Indian Railways is developing an indigenous signalling protocol for high-speed rail. The Bharat Train Control System (BTCS) is being designed specifically for Indian operating conditions. The system aims to eliminate dependence on foreign signalling protocols for the nearly 7,000 km of new bullet train corridors.

Article Title: India-US trade pact: Piyush Goyal explains the one condition to seal the deal
Article Text:
100% tariff threats



The long proposed India-US bilateral trade agreement will enter its first phase only after Washington restores India's tariff competitiveness against rival exporting nations,Addressing concerns around the much awaited trade pact, commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal on Wednesday, said that the understanding reached between the two countries was based on India receiving a comparative advantage over competing economies, including neighbouring countries and those in the ASEAN region.Once the condition is met again, the agreement would be ready to come into force.Addressing reporters, Goyal said, "I have categorically and on several occasions expressed the confidence that what we have finalized with the US as the first tranche of the bilateral trade agreement, which was announced by our leaders on 3rd of February, will come into operation as soon as the United States is able to ensure that we get a comparative advantage over our competitors, the countries in our neighborhood, the countries in the ASEAN region and other countries with whom we compete. "He added that India is confident of increasing its exports to the US market, provided its tariff treatment is favourable or at par with competing countries."For us, as long as we have comparative advantage or comparable duties, I think India will continue to grow its exports and continue to leverage the large US opportunity," he said.The minister also said India had participated in the Office of the United States Trade Representative's Section 301 investigations related to forced labour concerns.Under that probe, the US has imposed a 10% tariff on India.The minister’s remarks come as attention remains locked on a legislative proposal by the US administration that could allow tariffs to be imposed on countries purchasing Russian energy.The Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, introduced in the US Senate, would authorise the US President to impose tariffs of up to 100% on imports from major buyers of Russian crude oil and natural gas.However, the proposed legislation would not automatically result in tariffs.Under Section 113, Trump would have discretionary authority to decide whether tariffs should be imposed, determine the countries that would be covered and fix the applicable tariff rate.The proposal comes at a time when the US-Iran war has disrupted crude oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz. Middle Eastern suppliers, which account for a significant share of India's crude oil imports, have either reduced exports or altered shipping routes.To offset the shortfall, India has increased purchases of Russian crude oil, which was supported in part by the US sanctions waiver, which has since lapsed, although India has continued procuring Russian crude.According to the background information, India's imports of Russian crude reached a record 2.6 million barrels per day in June and are expected to average close to that level during July.On July 28, the US Senate voted 86-12 to invoke cloture, a procedural step that ends debate and allows the legislation to move to a final vote.
Article Summary: commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal on Wednesday, said that the understanding reached between the two countries was based on India receiving a comparative advantage over competing economies. Once the condition is met again, the agreement would be ready to come into force.

Article Title: E20 petrol debate: Govt debunks 7 claims on ethanol blended fuel - impact on mileage, engines & more
Article Text:
Manufacturers continue to provide warranty coverage for vehicles using specification-compliant E20 fuel.

We take a look at the 7-point clarification issued by the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas on E20 petrol and its impact:

Claim 1: Vehicles manufactured before 2023 cannot run on E20 petrol

Claim 2: 30 crore vehicles will become unusable

More than 20 crore two-wheelers and over 3 crore petrol cars have been running on these fuels.

There has been no verified evidence of widespread engine failure or vehicle breakdown linked to ethanol blending.

Claim 3: E20 not desirable by automobile manufacturers

Claim 4: Older vehicles are at risk

No abnormal corrosion linked to E20 fuel was observed.

No abnormal wear was reported.

No reduction in component life was attributed to E20 usage.

Ethanol blending: How India compares globally

Claim 5: Mileage will completely go down

Driving behaviour

Traffic conditions

Vehicle maintenance

Tyre pressure

Air-conditioner usage

A higher octane rating and improved anti-knock properties.

Cleaner combustion and smoother engine operation.

Better acceleration and overall driving performance.

Claim 6: Manufacturers are being forced to support E20.

Certified vehicles as E20-compatible.

Continued to honour warranty commitments for those vehicles.

Claim 7: Automobile companies are under government pressure to hide the truth about E20.

India's automobile manufacturers are independent, publicly listed companies with legal and regulatory responsibilities towards their customers.

Concealing widespread vehicle defects would expose them to warranty claims, product liability, regulatory action and significant reputational damage.

Manufacturers continue to honour warranties for E20-compatible vehicles, something they would not do if they believed E20 fuel was causing widespread engine damage. Their warranty decisions are based on engineering validation and real-world operating experience, not political considerations.

Seeking to dispel concerns about the impact of E20 petrol on vehicles, the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas has released a list of seven claims which it has rejected. From mileage and engine failure to compatibility, the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas has sought to dispel “misleading claims”.Meanwhile, Road Transport and Highways Minister Nitin Gadkari has said that petrol blended with 20% ethanol (E20) may lower fuel efficiency by 2-6%, depending on the type and age of the vehicle.In a written reply to the Lok Sabha, Gadkari said engine durability tests conducted both on dynamometers and under real-world driving conditions have not recorded any failures linked to the use of E20 fuel. He added that, compared with E10 petrol, E20 offers better acceleration, improved ride quality and around 30% lower carbon emissions.The minister said the impact of E20 on BS-III, BS-IV and BS-VI petrol-powered two-wheelers and four-wheelers was evaluated through a joint study carried out by the Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI), the Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM) and Indian Oil Corporation Ltd (IOCL).The government has said that vehicles that have been manufactured before 2023 can safely use E20 petrol.The release cites more than 3.5 years of E15+ use and over 2.5 years of E19-E20.Vehicles that have been using ethanol blended petrol for some years now show no verified evidence of widespread engine failures or vehicle breakdowns.The assessment is based on over 25 years of phased implementation, extensive testing and real-world data, including service records from 2.84 crore vehicles in FY2025-26, of which 1.5 crore were not originally E20-compatible, as well as data from another 1.4 crore E20-operated vehicles, all of which found no E20-related corrosion, abnormal wear or reduction in component life.The government has clarified that petrol blended with more than 15% ethanol (E15+) has been in widespread use for over three and a half years, while E19-E20 fuel has been available for more than two and a half years.During this period:“If E20 really rendered vehicles unusable, India would have witnessed millions of breakdowns, warranty claims and service campaigns. Nothing of that sort has occurred,” the release said.On July 4, 2026, the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas, together with the Ministry of Heavy Industries and the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways, held a joint press conference in which senior representatives from Toyota Kirloskar, Maruti Suzuki , Hero MotoCorp, Hyundai Motor India, TVS Motor Company and Bajaj Auto addressed concerns related to E20 fuel. The companies presented a unified position in support of the programme.Toyota said that the E20 was introduced only after rigorous testing under internationally recognised UNECE standards. Maruti Suzuki, citing service data from 2.84 crore vehicles in FY2025-26, including over 1.5 crore older vehicles, reported no E20-related corrosion, abnormal wear or reduction in component life, adding that the impact on fuel efficiency is generally limited to 3-3.5%.Hero MotoCorp also said its service data showed no higher incidence of damage in vehicles using E20, while the companies collectively reiterated their commitment to the programme and to addressing consumer concerns transparently.A leading automobile manufacturer serviced 2.84 crore vehicles during FY2025-26, including nearly 1.5 crore vehicles that were not originally certified as E20-compatible.According to the company's service data:A leading two-wheeler manufacturer has reported similar findings from its field experience. In addition, another automobile manufacturer tracked 1.4 crore vehicles operating on E20 over an extended period and found no evidence of ethanol-induced corrosion.The release cited government studies and data from automobile manufacturers that consistently indicate that fuel efficiency is influenced by several factors, including:For some older vehicles originally designed for E10 fuel, any reduction in fuel economy is generally limited to around 3-5%, rather than the much higher figures being circulated, the release said.At the same time the release claimed that, E20 fuel offers several performance advantages, including:The government said that if automobile manufacturers had not been satisfied with the scientific validation of E20 fuel, they would neither have:Manufacturers continue to provide warranty coverage for vehicles using specification-compliant E20 fuel because they are confident in the extensive testing and validation carried out before the fuel was introduced.In its clarification, the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas said:

Manufacturers continue to provide warranty coverage for vehicles using specification-compliant E20 fuel. Road Transport and Highways Minister Nitin Gadkari has said that petrol blended with 20% ethanol (E20) may lower fuel efficiency by 2-6%.

Article Title: Seeking job in US? Trump weighs $100,000 work permit fee from foreign graduates
Article Text:
A proposed $100,000 post-study work fee could make it significantly more expensive for international students to work in the US post graduation

The Trump administration is considering imposing a $100,000 fee on international students seeking to work in the United States after graduating from American universities, according to people familiar with the matter, in a move that could significantly reduce the appeal of studying in the country.The proposed fee would apply to the Optional Practical Training (OPT) programme, which allows international graduates to work in the US on their student visas for up to three years, depending on their field of study. Around 419,000 foreign graduates were working under the OPT programme in 2024, the latest available data show.If approved, the measure would mark another step in President Donald Trump's broader push to tighten legal immigration. It could also deal a blow to US universities, which rely heavily on international students for tuition revenue, and to technology and financial firms that recruit graduates from American universities for skilled roles.The proposal is still under discussion at the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), and it remains unclear whether the White House will approve it. Officials have also not decided whether the fee would be paid by international students themselves or by universities or employers hiring them.A DHS spokesperson said no policy should be considered final until it is formally announced."No policies should be considered final until formally announced. At DHS we are always having conversations about how to use all tools in our arsenal to protect the integrity of our legal immigration system," the spokesperson said.The proposed charge is expected to be linked to a new requirement announced earlier this month requiring international students to apply for an extension of their visas to access OPT. Previously, student visas remained valid through the duration of a student's academic programme and the associated work-authorisation period.The administration is also preparing a broader overhaul of the OPT programme, with revised regulations expected as early as this fall.The proposal follows the administration's earlier attempt to impose a $100,000 fee on H-1B visas for foreign professionals. That fee, announced last year, was blocked by a federal appeals court in Boston last week.While the H-1B levy was eventually narrowed to apply only to foreign professionals seeking to enter the US after facing opposition from major technology companies, a fee on OPT would more directly affect firms that recruit international graduates from American universities before transitioning them to H-1B visas.The $100,000 fee has emerged as a recurring feature of the administration's immigration agenda. Officials are also considering requiring green card applicants outside the US to post a refundable $100,000 bond that would be returned only after they become US citizens.The OPT programme has long been a key incentive for international students choosing to study in the United States. Supporters argue it enables graduates to gain professional experience before returning home or pursuing longer-term employment, while critics contend it allows employers to hire foreign graduates without sufficient safeguards to ensure wages remain comparable to those offered to American workers.During Trump's first term, senior immigration officials, including Stephen Miller, pushed to eliminate the STEM OPT programme, which provides eligible science, technology, engineering and mathematics graduates with up to three years of work authorisation. The proposal was ultimately shelved after opposition from business-oriented members of the administration, including Jared Kushner.
Article Summary: Proposed fee would apply to the Optional Practical Training (OPT) programme. Around 419,000 foreign graduates were working under the OPT programme in 2024. If approved, the measure would mark another step in President Donald Trump's broader push to tighten legal immigration.

Article Title: 5.9 crore returns filed till July 31 deadline: I-T dept
Article Text: NEW DELHI: The I-T department on Saturday said that 5.9 crore returns had been filed till July 31, the deadline for most individuals to make their annual filing.The number is lower than the over 7.3 crore returns that were filed by Sept 16, 2025, which was the extended deadline for filing last year. The numbers are likely to be lower as govt had announced major tax concessions during the last financial year, with income up to Rs 12 lakh.According to official data, including revised returns, 8.7 crore returns were filed by individuals in FY2024-25, with a little less than 8.1 crore return filers in the segment.“Your trust and timely compliance provide the energy that fuels India’s growth,” the Central Board of Direct Taxes said in a post on X. Those who have missed the deadline can still file returns till Dec but will have to shell out a penalty.Taxpayers who have business income and have to use ITR-3 can file returns up to Aug 31, while those using ITR-4 regime can file returns up to Oct 31.The I-T department’s numbers indicate returns were staggered over a period with no last-minute rush. Till late Friday morning, 5.5 crore returns had been filed with 42 lakh on Wednesday.
Article Summary: The number is lower than the over 7.3 crore returns that were filed by Sept 16, 2025. The numbers are likely to be lower as govt had announced major tax concessions during the last financial year. Those who have missed the deadline can still file returns till Dec but will have to shell out a penalty.

Article Title: UPI transactions touch Rs 76cr/day, FASTag declines
Article Text: MUMBAI: UPI transactions scaled new highs in July 2026, while NETC FASTag transactions declined on a year-on-year basis. UPI processed 2,366 crore transactions in July, up 4.1% from 2,272 crore in June. On a year-on-year basis, transaction count grew 22%. In contrast, NETC FASTag processed 34.7 crore transactions in July, down 4.1% from 36.2 crore in June and 6% a year earlier.The value of UPI transactions rose to Rs 29.88 lakh crore in July from Rs 28.92 lakh crore in June, an increase of 3.3%, but it was marginally below the Rs 29.9 lakh crore recorded in May.UPI handled an average of 76.3 crore transactions in July daily, up from 75.7 crore in June. The average daily transaction value stood at Rs 96,383 crore, almost unchanged from Rs 96,405 crore in June.The value of NETC FASTag transactions stood at Rs 7,143 crore in July, down 1% from Rs 7,215 crore in June. It was also lower than the Rs 7,308 crorein May. TNN
Article Summary: UPI processed 2,366 crore transactions in July, up 4.1% from 2,272 crore in June. On a year-on-year basis, transaction count grew 22%. In contrast, NETC FASTag processed 34.7 crore transactions. The value of UPI transactions rose to Rs 29.88 lakh crore in July.

Article Title: Capital One says anti-money laundering review led to closure of over 300 Trump Organization accounts
Article Text:
Trump had claimed that blocking was politcally motivated

US President Donald Trump's family business Trump Organization has been accused by Capital One of having its bank accounts closed following an internal anti-money laundering (AML) review, according to a court filing amid ongoing legal battle.In a court filing on Friday, the bank said the account closures were the result of "months of analysis and a careful review" conducted by its AML experts in line with internal policies and regulatory guidance and not politically motivated, as reported by Reuters."Documents and Plaintiffs' own allegations make clear that Capital One closed Plaintiffs' accounts for anti-money laundering ('AML') reasons," the filing said.The accounts were held by the Trump Organization, the privately owned business conglomerate that oversees Trump's hotels, golf courses, real estate and other ventures. Large companies often operate hundreds of bank accounts across different entities and properties. US banks can close customer accounts after internal compliance and risk reviews if they determine the banking relationship no longer meets their anti-money laundering or regulatory standards.Capital One did not directly accuse the Trump Organization of engaging in illegal money laundering. Instead, it argued that the decision was based on compliance and risk assessment procedures, not political considerations.The filing marks the first time a bank has formally stated in court that anti-money laundering concerns were behind its decision to close the Trump Organization's accounts.The bank is seeking dismissal of a lawsuit filed by the Trump Organization and Eric Trump in March 2025 in a Florida federal court. The lawsuit alleges that Capital One closed the accounts because of its "woke" beliefs and to align with the political climate following the January 6, 2021, attack on the US Capitol.Capital One notified the Trump Organization in March 2021 that it would close more than 300 affiliated accounts.The federal court in Miami has already dismissed two versions of the lawsuit while allowing the plaintiffs to amend their complaint. In Friday's filing, Capital One argued that the latest complaint "suffers from the same fundamental flaws" as the previous versions.The bank described the allegations of political bias as "misguided" and said they were "based on cherry-picked quotations unsupported by the full context" of documents submitted to the court."The transaction patterns identified by Capital One are among the types of activity flagged by federal banking guidance," the filing said.The dispute comes as the Trump administration has intensified scrutiny of alleged "debanking" by major financial institutions. Trump signed an executive order in August 2025 barring discriminatory debanking and, earlier this year, filed a separate lawsuit against JPMorgan Chase on similar grounds.The Trump Organization and Eric Trump sued Capital One in March 2025, alleging the bank unlawfully closed more than 300 of their accounts in 2021 because of its "woke" beliefs and to align with the political climate following the January 6, 2021, attack on the US Capitol. They argued the closures amounted to discriminatory "debanking" and sought damages.
Article Summary: Bank says account closures were result of "months of analysis and a careful review" The bank is seeking dismissal of a lawsuit filed by the Trump Organization and Eric Trump. The lawsuit alleges that Capital One closed the accounts because of its "woke" beliefs and to align with the political climate.

Article Title: Passenger vehicle sales hit top gear as July dispatches jump 33%; Maruti, Hyundai set records
Article Text:
Maruti and Hyundai set new records



Momentum remains strong



India's passenger vehicle industry is estimated to have posted one of its strongest monthly performances in July, with domestic dispatches rising by around 33% year-on-year to nearly 4.7 lakh units. Strong volumes from leading manufacturers, including Maruti Suzuki and Hyundai, along with robust growth reported by Tata Motors and Mahindra & Mahindra, helped drive the industry's expansion during the month.The sustained momentum came as automakers continued to benefit from demand-supporting measures introduced over the past year, including GST 2.0, lower repo rates and income tax relief for individuals earning up to Rs 12 lakh."Industry (passenger vehicle sales) should be around 4.65 lakh to 4.7 lakh in July this year. In July last year, the industry was around 3.5 lakh, so it is almost a growth of 33%," Maruti Suzuki India Ltd (MSIL) senior executive officer, marketing & sales, Partho Banerjee, told reporters in a conference call.Explaining the factors supporting the market, Banerjee said GST 2.0, repo rate cuts and income tax relief for entry-level customers had continued to boost demand since last year."Fundamentally, these three tailwinds are very much there," Banerjee noted.Maruti Suzuki led the market with its highest-ever domestic passenger vehicle sales of 1,96,203 units in July, compared with 1,37,776 units in the same month last year, registering a growth of 43.4%. "The company has witnessed all-round growth across segments from entry-level small cars to SUVs in July," Banerjee said, adding that alternate fuel CNG models continue to have robust demand.Hyundai Motor India Ltd (HMIL) achieved its best-ever domestic monthly sales since inception, dispatching 54,210 units in July, up 23.3% from a year ago. "Our highest-ever monthly volume since inception, underscores the immense trust consumers place in brand Hyundai," HMIL MD & CEO Tarun Garg said.Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Ltd (TMPVL) also reported one of the steepest gains among major carmakers, with domestic passenger vehicle sales jumping 58% to 62,611 units in July from 39,521 units in the corresponding month last year.Mahindra & Mahindra followed the suit, posting healthy growth, with domestic utility vehicle sales rising 20% to 60,048 units from 49,871 units a year earlier.At the same time, Honda Cars India Ltd (HCIL) recorded domestic sales of 6,014 units during the month, reflecting growth of more than 48% over July last year.Apart from Indian auto giants, global car manufacturers also registered strong growth. Toyota Kirloskar Motor posted domestic sales of 30,516 units in July, up 5% from 29,159 units in the same month of 2025.Kia India registered wholesale dispatches of 28,200 units, marking a 27.4% increase over 22,135 units a year ago. The company said it was its best-ever July wholesale performance since inception.JSW MG Motor India also reported its highest-ever monthly wholesale volumes, dispatching 8,158 units to dealers during the month, up 22% year-on-year.Nissan Motor India Pvt Ltd (NMIPL) more than tripled its domestic wholesale volumes, reporting 4,518 units in July compared with 1,420 units in the same month last year.
Article Summary: India's passenger vehicle industry is estimated to have posted one of its strongest monthly performances in July. Domestic dispatches rose by around 33% year-on-year to nearly 4.7 lakh units. Strong volumes from leading manufacturers, including Maruti Suzuki and Hyundai, along with robust growth.

Article Title: Zepto to raise funds amid delayed listing
Article Text: MUMBAI: Zepto on Saturday said that it will raise funds through a pre-IPO financing amid tepid response from investors to its public listing.Zepto did not share the specifics of the transaction but said that the move will strengthen its balance sheet. It is looking to raise around Rs 1,000 crore through the round at a valuation of $4-4.5 billion, sharply lower than its last valuation of $7 billion, TOI had reported.On Friday, co-founder & CEO Aadit Palicha had told employees that the company will defer its IPO by two to three quarters. The startup which was initially eyeing a listing around July has stalled the process after domestic investors valued it at $3-3.5 billion.
Article Summary: Zepto did not share the specifics of the transaction but said that the move will strengthen its balance sheet. The startup which was initially eyeing a listing around July has stalled the process after domestic investors valued it at $3-3.5 billion.

Article Title: July auto sales rev up as Maruti crosses 2L, Tata EVs double
Article Text: NEW DELHI: New model launches, led almost entirely by sport utility vehicles, helped several automakers post record July sales, suggesting that in an otherwise competitive passenger vehicle market, fresh products are increasingly deciding the winners. Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles registered the strongest growth among the larger manufacturers, with sales jumping 59% year-on-year to 63,760 units.While Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles electric vehicle sales more than doubled to 15,217 units, the company has also expanded its SUV portfolio over the past year.Market leader Maruti Suzuki sold 2.4 lakh vehicles in July, up from 1.8 lakh units a year earlier. Domestic sales crossed the two-lakh mark for the first time in any July, while utility vehicle sales surged nearly 50% to 78,851 units, reflecting the growing contribution of models such as the Fronx, Grand Vitara, Brezza and electric Vitara.Mahindra continued to ride the SUV wave, retailing 60,048 utility vehicles in the domestic market, up 20% year-on-year. Including exports, SUV sales stood at 60,887 units, while overall vehicle sales rose 26% to 1,03,860 units. Exports climbed 47% to 4,070 units.Meanwhile, Hyundai Motor India and Kia India also posted their best-ever July wholesale volumes, driven by their SUV line-ups.Hyundai has reported record monthly sales of 75,360 units, including 54,210 domestic sales and 21,150 exports - its highest export tally in more than 100 months.Kia dispatched 28,200 units, up 27.4% from a year earlier, saying demand remained strong for the Seltos and Sonet, while newer models such as the Syros and Carens Clavis added to growth.Among other automobile manufacturers, JSW MG Motor India posted its second consecutive record monthly wholesale performance, dispatching 8,158 vehicles, with electric vehicles contributing over 80% of sales.Meanwhile, the clearest impact of a new launch was most visible at Nissan.Domestic wholesales soared 218% to 4,518 units after deliveries of the Tekton SUV began on July 20. Including exports, the company sold 9,339 vehicles, riding on the launch of the Tekton.
Article Summary: Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles registered the strongest growth among the larger manufacturers. Mahindra continued to ride the SUV wave, retailing 60,048 utility vehicles in the domestic market. Hyundai Motor India and Kia India also posted their best-ever July wholesale volumes.

Article Title: UPI reaches new milestone in July with highest-ever transaction value of Rs 29.88 lakh crore
Article Text:
Stronger digital payment ecosystem



UPI expands its global footprint



India's Unified Payments Interface (UPI) continued its upward trajectory in July, clocking its highest-ever monthly transaction value. According to data released by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI), the platform touched a new peak in transaction volumes, while the value of transactions reached Rs 29.88 lakh crore in July.The platform processed 23.66 billion transactions during the month, exceeding the 22.72 billion recorded in June and the previous high of 23.2 billion in May. On an annual basis, the value of UPI transactions rose 19% from Rs 25.08 lakh crore in July last year to Rs 29.88 lakh crore this year.The latest figures indicate sustained growth in the use of UPI for digital payments. While transaction volumes stood at 22.72 billion in June, they rose to 23.66 billion in July. Earlier, May had recorded 23.2 billion transactions.The July transaction value also surpassed the record level seen in May 2026, when UPI transactions had touched Rs 29.9 lakh crore.Reacting to the latest data, PayNearby managing director and chief executive officer Anand Kumar Bajaj said, "UPI continues to strengthen the foundation of India's digital payments ecosystem. In July 2026, it processed 23.66 billion transactions worth Rs 29.88 lakh crore, reaffirming its role as the preferred mode of payment for millions of Indians."He said the next phase of growth should focus on increasing confidence and accessibility among users across the country."As UPI adoption deepens, the focus must remain on building trust, awareness and ease of usage at the grassroots, " he said, adding that strengthening these foundations will be essential to ensuring that the growth of digital payments translates into wider and more meaningful financial inclusion across Bharat.UPI is now operational in about 10 countries, including the UAE, Singapore, Bhutan, Nepal, Sri Lanka, France, Mauritius and Qatar.According to the inputs, the platform's growing international adoption is boosting remittances, promoting financial inclusion and strengthening India's position in the global fintech landscape.The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI), an initiative of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and the Indian Banks' Association (IBA), is the umbrella organisation for operating retail payments and settlement systems in the country.It operates UPI, which enables real-time payments between individuals as well as payments made to merchants while making purchases.
Article Summary: UPI processed 23.66 billion transactions during the month, exceeding the 22.72 billion recorded in June and the previous high of 23.2 billion in May. The value of UPI transactions rose 19% from Rs 25.08 lakh crore in July last year to Rs 29.88 lakh crore this year.

Article Title: Indian equities ‘probably oversold’: Foreign investors warm up to India after months of outflows
Article Text:
Geopolitics and oil remain key risks



RBI may stay aligned with the Fed



Bloomberg bond index delay



Global liquidity shaping bond allocations



After months of sustained selling, foreign investors are beginning to turn more positive on India, with equities now "probably oversold", Motilal Oswal Financial Services chairman Raamdeo Agrawal said on Saturday, even as he warned that geopolitical uncertainties and elevated oil prices continue to cloud the outlook.Speaking to news agency ANI, Agrawal said that a large amount of foreign portfolio investor (FPI) capital had already left India over the past two years, making the recent shift in sentiment noteworthy."In the last two years already we have lost a lot of FPI capital. They've been completely on the outflow, particularly this year... Clearly, a lot of capital has left the country," he said.According to Agrawal, the prolonged outflows were driven by a mix of factors, including domestic market valuations, stronger returns in other global markets and the lack of a strong artificial intelligence investment theme in India. He added that geopolitical tensions had also kept oil prices high, putting pressure on India's external position.However, he said the trend had started to change over the past week."We are seeing for the last one week... a reversal of trend where FIIs are actually looking at India more favourably. Probably they are oversold. That's the situation right now," he said.While foreign investor sentiment appears to be improving, Agrawal said global developments would continue to determine the direction of markets."How geopolitics will shape up, only time will tell. Who knows what's going to happen in Iran? What's going to happen to oil prices?" he said.Despite these uncertainties, he maintained that India's domestic economy continues to perform well, pointing to healthy automobile sales, strong GST collections and robust credit growth."I think the domestic economy is booming. I would say there is a good pickup in the economy... The credit flow is about 18 per cent or so. On the back of that, we are doing very well, except that the forex situation is a little dicey because of oil prices and whatever is happening geopolitically," he said.On monetary policy, Agrawal said he expects the Reserve Bank of India to broadly remain on the same path as the US Federal Reserve."Since the US has kept the rate on pause, I would think that we also follow the same trajectory," he said, while adding that he was "not a student of monetary economics."He also cautioned that the sharp rise in credit growth compared with last year could create short-term inflationary pressures."Last year it was more like 9-10 per cent kind of credit growth. Now we are running at 17-18 per cent kind of credit growth... They may have to moderate the credit growth to control inflation in the short term," he said.Agrawal also weighed in on Bloomberg's decision to defer the inclusion of Indian Government Securities (G-Secs) in its Global Aggregate Bond Index, saying the move reflects a cautious approach by global benchmark providers rather than concerns over India's sovereign debt."In the backdrop of global macroeconomic shifts and evolving benchmark considerations, top financial market experts expressed confidence that the delay in the inclusion of Indian Government Securities (G-Secs) in Bloomberg's Global Aggregate Bond Index reflects tactical and global market dynamics rather than any fundamental flaw in India's sovereign debt story.""India remains on the watchlist. Even though these are Indian government bonds, global benchmark providers take a short-term, cautious assessment to ensure operational systems and market mechanisms function smoothly before full execution," Agrawal told ANI.He said that despite volatility in global capital flows and portfolio realignments by foreign investors, India's domestic economic fundamentals and market structure remain resilient.Echoing a similar view, Ashish Shanker, MD & CEO of Motilal Oswal Private Wealth, said that the delay in index inclusion should be seen in the context of broader global liquidity conditions and investor sentiment towards emerging markets."Right now, it does reflect broader concerns towards emerging markets. Look at what is happening in the background - even in the US, companies are becoming leveraged... with the massive spending witnessed in the AI space, especially in data centres, most of these companies will run low on cash over time. That will put upward pressure on yields across the world," he said.Shanker said global interest rate cycles are likely to remain elevated, but added that India's debt market remains well placed to attract foreign capital over the longer term."Yields will not come down easily, but India is at a slightly advantageous position because we could see more FPI flows in the near term," Shanker added, while advising domestic debt investors to focus on simple three-to-five-year Target Maturity products and high-rated G-Secs.Market veterans at MOBIC 2026 said that although foreign institutional investors regularly rebalance their portfolios across global markets, temporary delays in benchmark index inclusion are unlikely to alter the long-term structural flow of foreign capital into India's debt markets.
Article Summary: Foreign investors are beginning to turn more positive on India, Motilal Oswal Financial Services chairman Raamdeo Agrawal said on Saturday. But he warned that geopolitical uncertainties and elevated oil prices continue to cloud the outlook. He also weighed in on Bloomberg's decision to defer the inclusion of Indian Government Securities (G-Secs) in its Global Aggregate Bond Index.

Article Title: Zepto to raise pre-IPO funding amid delayed listing
Article Text:
Zepto to raise pre-IPO funding amid delayed listing﻿

MUMBAI: Zepto on Saturday said that it will raise funds through a pre-IPO financing amid tepid response from investors to its public listing. The startup did not share the specifics of the transaction but said that the move will strengthen its balance sheet. The company is looking to raise about Rs 1,000 crore (about $105 million) through the round at a valuation of $4-4.5 billion, sharply lower than its last valuation of $7 billion, TOI had reported.On Friday, co-founder & CEO Aadit Palicha told employees that the company will defer its IPO by two to three quarters. The startup which was initially eyeing a listing around July has stalled the process after domestic investors valued it at $3-3.5 billion, with some of them even valuing it at $2.5 billion.“Zepto has agreed with major shareholders to close a pre-IPO private placement of equity ahead of its planned listing. This pre-IPO financing will add to the company’s strong balance sheet (5,681 crores of cash with no debt as of March 31, 2026). As part of the IPO process, the board and founders have received terms from public market investors to list the company and are appreciative of the expressed interest. However, at this time, and afforded by the company's strong balance sheet, Zepto will focus on continued execution,” the company said in a statement.The company was initially targeting to raise up to Rs 8,010 crore through a fresh issue of shares.The competitive landscape of the quick commerce space has changed after Amazon and Flipkart’s foray into the segment. Both the deep-pocketed companies are aggressively expanding their operations, stoking investor concerns. Zepto’s losses stood at Rs 5,905 crore as of FY26. In June, BofA Securities had said that at its current rate of cash burn (Q4FY26), the startup is roughly estimated to have about three quarters of runway left.
Article Summary: Zepto is looking to raise about Rs 1,000 crore (about $105 million) through the round at a valuation of $4-4.5 billion. Co-founder & CEO Aadit Palicha told employees that the company will defer its IPO by two to three quarters.

Article Title: Samudra Manthan explained: How India’s offshore oil & gas exploration scheme can be a game-changer
Article Text:
Samudra Manthan scheme expected to add over 600 MMTOE of reserves and will be implemented through FY 2030-31. (Representative image)

“To make the country developed, we are now moving towards ‘

Samudra Manthan

’ (churning of the ocean). Taking forward our Samudra Manthan, we want to work in a mission mode towards finding oil reserves, gas reserves under the sea and hence India is going to start the National Deep Water Exploration Mission

,”

What is Samudra Manthan – National Offshore Exploration Scheme?

What is the Samudra Manthan scheme?

Large-scale acquisition, processing and interpretation of high-quality seismic data.

Accelerated deepwater and ultra-deepwater exploratory drilling.

Scientific drilling in frontier basins.

Development of common offshore production and evacuation infrastructure.

Creation of an integrated Oil & Gas Manufacturing and Services Zone.

Digital programme management, capacity building, technology adoption, stakeholder engagement and international outreach.

Expected to add more than 600 Million Metric Tons of Oil Equivalent (MMTOE) to India's reserves.

Aims to significantly expand offshore exploration and increase domestic oil and gas production.

India’s exposure to oil and gas imports



India's Oil & Gas Exploration: The Big Picture

Importance of upstream output

Significance of ‘Samudra Manthan’

How the scheme can expand

Challenges and road ahead

Crude dependence unlikely to come down soon

On August 15, 2025, Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke of energy security, announcing the National Deep Water Exploration Mission.PM Modi said from the ramparts of Red Fort.Six months later, India’s energy security saw one of its biggest tests in recent times with the start of the Middle East conflict. It was an unprecedented oil shock and India, which is largely dependent on the world for its oil, LPG, and LNG needs, saw its economy staring at a grim situation.Since then the US-Iran war has subsided and India has also managed to ensure its energy security through a vastly diversified supply chain. But the reality of the dependence remains, and so does the vulnerability.In this backdrop, the Union Cabinet’s decision to approve the Rs 84,084 crore Samudra Manthan – National Offshore Exploration Scheme is being seen as a strategic and possibly game-changing move.The Samudra Manthan – National Offshore Exploration Scheme aims to unlock India’s offshore oil and gas potential. This will be done through large-scale seismic surveys, deepwater exploration, scientific drilling, shared offshore infrastructure and an integrated manufacturing ecosystem.The scheme is expected to add over 600 Million Metric Tons of Oil Equivalent (MMTOE) of reserves and will be implemented through FY 2030-31.Some of the key aspects of the scheme include:India is a major oil importer with nearly 90% of its crude oil needs being met through imports. The dependence came to stark light amid the US-Iran conflict when closure of Strait of Hormuz left India vulnerable to an oil and gas supply shock. Even as it swiftly diversified its procurement basket, what was obvious was the lack of its own supply.With this backdrop, the Samudra Manthan scheme assumes greater significance.As Sourav Mitra, Partner - Oil & Gas, Grant Thornton Bharat points out: India has built a meaningful exploration platform, but its upstream output remains well below the country’s hydrocarbon requirement.As of July 2026, 172 blocks covering nearly 3.8 lakh square kilometres had been awarded under the Open Acreage Licensing Programme, with committed investment exceeding $4.3 billion; around 674 wells were drilled in FY 2025-26. Nearly 99% of the erstwhile offshore “No-Go” areas have also been opened for exploration. Yet the supply gap remains substantial, he tells TOI.As per the Petroleum Planning & Analysis Cell (PPAC), domestic crude oil production stood at 28.71 million tonnes in FY 2025-26, while crude oil import dependence reached 88.7%.“More importantly, domestic production remains on a downward trajectory: crude oil production declined by 2.8% in FY 2025-26, and the decline has continued into FY 2026-27, with production falling by a further 4.2% year-on-year during April–May 2026. Natural gas shows a similar, though less severe, imbalance: PNGRB reports 34,326 MMSCM of domestic production against 68,542 MMSCM of consumption in FY2025-26, with LNG imports accounting for about half of consumption,” Mitra tells TOI.However, this should be distinguished from India’s downstream capability. India has 258.1 million tonnes per annum of refining capacity, compared with 243.2 million tonnes of domestic petroleum-product consumption in FY 2025-26, while exports stood at 61.5 million tonnes in the same year.“In other words, refining capacity is not the principal constraint; domestic feedstock availability is. The demand gap is structural. The IEA expects India to add about one million barrels per day of oil demand by 2030, taking consumption to 6.66 million barrels per day – growth larger than India’s entire present domestic supply. India therefore needs not merely more acreage, but stronger conversion of geological data, drilling and discoveries into commercially producing fields,” Mitra explains.Experts see the Samudra Manthan scheme as a significant strategic initiative for India's upstream sector. They believe it reflects a shift from simply managing import dependence to actively expanding domestic resource development. It is also being seen as an unambiguous signal that domestic offshore exploration is a key national priority.“The scheme's focus on large-scale seismic acquisition, deepwater and ultra-deepwater exploration, common offshore infrastructure and technology adoption should improve exploration efficiency and encourage greater investment in India's offshore basins. If successful, it has the potential to increase domestic oil and gas production, strengthen the domestic oilfield services industry and enhance India's long-term energy security,” says Sumit Ritolia, Lead analyst, Modelling and Refining at Kpler.India hasn't made a discovery of the scale of Mumbai High or the Krishna-Godavari basin or the Barmer basin in decades.Rajnish Gupta, Partner, Tax and Economic Policy Group, EY India notes that only a fraction of our sedimentary basin area is meaningfully explored. Vast stretches remain effectively untouched. This, set against import dependence of over 85% for crude oil and 50% for natural gas is the issue that this scheme is designed to address.“The most significant elements are the commitment to large-scale seismic data acquisition and the push into deepwater and ultra-deepwater frontier basins, the areas where exploration risk is the highest. Availability of seismic data and together with exploratory well logs are precisely the geological data that can de-risk exploration activities. Shared infrastructure for production and evacuation can lower the breakeven for blocks that may otherwise be seen as marginal,” he explains.According to Gupta, what makes this especially significant is the multiplier effect good data can have. Data is not just important for the government but can unlock private capital.“If this exploration push turns up compelling results or if it opens up even new basins or play, that could trigger a wave of private and international investment well beyond the scheme's own outlay. A single strong discovery, or even strong indicative data, can pull the industry's attention toward a basin overnight,” he tells TOI.“This is an important policy announcement and along with previous announcements like coal gasification or opening up of the nuclear sector or the recent Urea policy or the recent PLIs for the electronic sector signals that the government is keen to de-risk the economy and build greater resilience in the Indian economy,” he adds.The project is a big step, albeit a long-term one with a long gestation period. Hence it should be viewed as a long-term structural initiative rather than a near-term supply solution.According to Sourav Mitra, the principal challenge will lie in converting the exploration activity into commercially viable production.Offshore projects are capital-intensive, technologically complex, exposed to geological uncertainty and typically have long appraisal-to-production timelines.“India drilled around 674 wells in FY 2025-26, while five new discoveries were made and seven discoveries were monetised, underscoring that activity alone does not guarantee commercial outcomes,” he cautions.“The scheme will deliver the greatest value if funding is tightly stage-gated, environmental and safety standards remain rigorous, and success is measured by commercially recoverable discoveries, private investment mobilised and speed from discovery to production not simply by seismic kilometres acquired or wells drilled,” he adds.Experts point out that offshore exploration projects typically require several years to progress from seismic surveys and drilling to commercial production.As a result, India's crude import dependence is unlikely to decline materially over the next 5–10 years.“The immediate challenge remains securing reliable crude imports amid geopolitical disruptions, while this scheme lays the foundation for gradually reducing import dependence over the longer term,” says Kpler’s Ritolia.“If implemented effectively, it could also diversify India's domestic production base and improve resilience against future supply shocks, but execution, commercial discoveries and timely infrastructure development will ultimately determine its success,” he tells TOI.Experts say that the expected contribution should be viewed as a medium- to long-term reduction in import exposure, rather than an immediate substitute for a defined share of India’s oil demand.“The Cabinet expects Samudra Manthan to catalyse more than 600 MMTOE of reserve accretion. Importantly, MMTOE is an oil-equivalent measure covering both oil and gas, and the announcement provides no oil-gas split or annual production profile. It would therefore be premature to claim that the scheme will meet a specific percentage of India’s oil requirement,” says Grant Thornton Bharat’s Mitra.The Samudra Manthan theme is clearly an important step for India as it looks at securing its energy needs through a mix of domestic production, renewable energy push, and diversification of supply chain.Any commercially viable domestic production resulting from the programme would reduce, at the margin, exposure to imported crude, shipping constraints, foreign-exchange volatility and geopolitical disruption.And that resilience matters in the current market.“The IEA’s July 2026 Oil Market Report said global oil supply recovered to 98.8 million barrels per day in June but remained 9.4 million barrels per day below pre-war levels. However, the scheme runs through FY2030-31, and offshore discoveries require appraisal and development before production. Its strongest contribution will therefore be structural and cumulative; near-term energy security will still depend on diversified import sources, strategic reserves, refinery flexibility and substitution,” Mitra concludes.
Article Summary: The Samudra Manthan – National Offshore Exploration Scheme aims to unlock India’s offshore oil and gas potential. It will be done through large-scale seismic surveys, deepwater exploration, scientific drilling, shared offshore infrastructure and an integrated manufacturing ecosystem. The scheme is expected to add more than 600 Million Metric Tons of Oil Equivalent to India's reserves.

Article Title: Indian Oil ramps up spot crude purchases as Middle East disruptions hit supplies
Article Text:
Higher crude prices hit June profit

Supply disruptions in the Middle East have prompted Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) to overhaul its crude sourcing strategy, with the state-run refiner sharply increasing purchases from the spot market. The share of spot buying has risen from 50% to nearly 84%, IOC director (finance) Anuj Jain said on Saturday.The move comes after supplies through the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea were disrupted following the start of the US-Iran war in late February, pushing Indian refiners towards spot purchases."Our spot volume jumped from 50% to almost 84%, and the situation is very very dynamic...we keep track of the development on a day-to-day basis and try to optimize our crude sourcing," Jain said, as cited by Reuters.IOC, which depends heavily on spot purchases of Russian crude, has also increased imports from West African and Latin American producers to make up for the disruption in supplies from the Middle East, Jain stated.Along with its subsidiary Chennai Petroleum Corporation, IOC accounts for about one-third of India's 5.2 million barrels per day of refining capacity. The company is also moving ahead with plans to expand its refining business.Jain added that IOC aims to process 1.7 million barrels of crude oil per day at its directly owned refineries in 2027-28. The company expects to expand the capacity of some refinery units by the end of this year.The comments came a day after IOC reported a standalone net loss of Rs 2,661 crore for the April-June quarter, compared with a net profit of Rs 5,689 crore in the same period last year. Revenue from operations, however, rose 26% year-on-year to Rs 2,75,972 crore from Rs 2,18,608 crore.In a press release issued on Friday, Indian Oil said, "Decrease in Profitability is mainly on account of rise in crude cost due to West Asia conflict."Even as profits came under pressure, IOC posted its highest-ever first-quarter crude throughput of 19.165 million metric tonnes (MMT), up 3% from 18.683 MMT a year earlier. Refinery capacity utilisation improved to 109.4% from 106.7%, while fuel and loss dropped to a record low of 8.04% in the post-BS VI era.The company's cross-country pipeline network also recorded its highest-ever quarterly throughput at 28.548 MMT, up 9% from 26.256 MMT in the year-ago quarter. Petroleum sales rose 1% to 22.542 MMT during the quarter. IOC said its domestic market share increased to 43.1% from 41.5% a year ago. Sales of petrol (MS) and diesel (HSD) also reached record quarterly highs of 4.522 MMT and 10.866 MMT, respectively.Natural gas sales increased 11% year-on-year to 1.873 MMT from 1.685 MMT. The petrochemicals business reported better profitability, helped by higher sales of products such as LAB, BA, PTA and butadiene, while profit from the gas business also increased significantly during the quarter.
Article Summary: IOC's share of spot buying has risen from 50% to nearly 84%, IOC director (finance) Anuj Jain said. The move comes after supplies through the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea were disrupted following the start of the US-Iran war in late February.

Article Title: Forex boost: RBI's special swap facility draws $40.8 billion in foreign inflows by July-end
Article Text:
Facility to remain open until year-end



Foreign currency inflows under the Reserve Bank of India 's (RBI) special swap facility almost doubled in just two weeks, rising to $40.816 billion by July 31 from $20.718 billion as of July 17. According to the latest RBI data, Foreign Currency Non-Resident (Bank) [FCNR(B)] deposits remained the biggest contributor, accounting for the bulk of funds mobilised under the concessional swap scheme.The numbers are based on data received from Authorised Dealer Banks and reflect foreign exchange inflows raised through the RBI's special facility. According to the RBI, FCNR(B) deposits contributed $36.725 billion by the end of July, making them the largest source of funds under the facility. Overseas Foreign Currency Borrowings (OFCBs) accounted for $2.575 billion, while External Commercial Borrowings (ECBs) added $1.516 billion.With $36.725 billion mobilised through FCNR(B) deposits, this route accounted for around 90% of the total inflows under the facility. Between July 17 and July 31, total inflows under the scheme increased by $20.098 billion, or around 97%. The rise was driven primarily by FCNR(B) deposits, which increased by $19.319 billion during the two-week period, climbing from $17.406 billion to $36.725 billion.During the same period, inflows through OFCBs rose by $605 million, while ECBs increased by $174 million.As of July 17, the RBI had reported total inflows of $20.718 billion under the facility. These comprised $17.406 billion through FCNR(B) deposits, $1.970 billion through OFCBs and $1.342 billion through ECBs.The latest figures indicate that inflows have almost doubled within a fortnight as the central bank's measures to encourage foreign currency inflows continued to draw a robust response.The RBI had announced the concessional swap facility on June 5, 2026, as part of a series of measures aimed at strengthening India's balance of payments and encouraging capital inflows."With a view to strengthening our balance of payments and incentivising capital inflows, the RBI had announced a series of measures, including a facility for offering concessional swaps for fresh FCNR(B) deposits, OFCB and ECB inflows on June 5, 2026," the central bank said.The facility became operational on June 8, 2026.Under the current timelines, the special window for fresh FCNR(B) deposits will remain open until September 30, 2026, while concessional swaps for OFCBs and ECBs will continue until December 31, 2026.The measures were introduced as part of the RBI's efforts to strengthen the country's external sector position and support foreign exchange liquidity amid global market uncertainties. When the scheme was announced, initial estimates suggested it could mobilise as much as $70 billion in foreign exchange.
Article Summary: Foreign currency inflows under the Reserve Bank of India's special swap facility almost doubled in just two weeks, rising to $40.816 billion by July 31 from $20.718 billion as of July 17. Foreign Currency Non-Resident (Bank) [FCNR(B)] deposits remained the biggest contributor, accounting for the bulk of funds mobilised under the concessional swap scheme.

Article Title: GST collections jump 15.4% to over Rs 2.11 lakh crore in July
Article Text:
GST collections rise to over Rs 2.11 lakh crore, driven by imports and domestic demand

NEW DELHI: India's gross Goods and Services Tax (GST) collections rose 15.4 per cent year-on-year to over Rs 2.11 lakh crore in July, driven by higher revenues from both domestic transactions and imports, according to government data released on Friday.Gross GST collections stood at Rs 1.83 lakh crore in July 2025, while the Centre had collected around Rs 1.95 lakh crore in June 2026, making July the second consecutive month in which collections remained above the Rs 2 lakh crore mark.The July collections comprised Rs 39,835 crore from Central GST (CGST), Rs 47,881 crore from State GST (SGST), and over Rs 1.23 lakh crore from Integrated GST (IGST), reflecting strong tax inflows from inter-state transactions and imports.The government also continued to maintain a healthy pace of refunds. Total GST refunds rose 13.1 per cent year-on-year to Rs 29,968 crore in July.After adjusting for refunds, net GST revenue stood at over Rs 1.81 lakh crore, indicating sustained growth in the indirect tax base despite higher refund payouts.Abhishek Jain, Indirect Tax Head & Partner, KPMG said, ”July’s GST collections have come in strong, and the momentum looks healthy.Much of the growth this month was driven by imports; though it’s worth digging into whether that’s finished goods or raw materials, and how much of it simply reflects a weaker rupee rather than higher volumes. Domestic collections have grown steadily too, and with refunds also rising and there being fiscal headroom possibly, this may be a good moment to start thinking about a GST 3.0 - specifically refunds on input services for inverted duty structure companies. ”Manoj Mishra, Partner and Tax Controversy Management Leader, Grant Thornton Bharat feels that the GST collections are a compelling vote of confidence in India’s economic resilience.“The defining feature is the 28.8% surge in import GST —consistent with total imports expanding 26.85% in June and amplified by rupee depreciation, which increased the taxable rupee value of imported energy, commodities and industrial inputs. Continuing US–Iran hostilities and disruption across critical West Asian energy and shipping corridors have further elevated oil, freight and landed costs. Yet this is not solely an import-price story: domestic GST grew a robust 10.1%, reflecting resilient household consumption, formalisation and industrial activity. Strong gains across Maharashtra, Gujarat, Karnataka, Haryana, Telangana and Uttar Pradesh confirm broad-based momentum across India’s largest manufacturing, services and consumption hubs. India’s domestic economy continues to expand despite formidable global pressures,” he says.The latest figures build on the strong momentum seen in June, when gross GST collections increased 13.9 per cent year-on-year to Rs 1,94,812 crore, compared with Rs 1,71,105 crore in the same month last year. Net GST revenue in June had risen 11.2 per cent to Rs 1,62,377 crore.June's growth was largely driven by a sharp rise in import-related tax collections. GST revenue from imports surged 34.6 per cent year-on-year to Rs 60,038 crore, while domestic GST collections increased 6.5 per cent to Rs 1,34,774 crore. Refunds during the month also rose 29.1 per cent to Rs 32,436 crore, improving liquidity for businesses while keeping overall tax collections robust.
Article Summary: India's gross Goods and Services Tax (GST) collections rose 15.4 per cent year- on-year to over Rs 2.11 lakh crore in July. The July collections comprised Rs 39,835 crore from Central GST, Rs 47,881 crore from State GST, and over Rs 1.23 lakh crore from Integrated GST.

Article Title: 'Buy $5-10 billion yen': Bessent's 'to-do' note hints at US plan to back Japanese currency
Article Text:
Joint intervention

Japan steps up currency defence

The latest addition to the United State’s to-do list is Japanese currency, yen.Signs that Washington was preparing to back Japan's currency came to light on Friday after a photograph from US President Donald Trump's cabinet meeting at Camp David showed US treasury secretary Scott Bessent weighing purchases of between $5 billion and $10 billion worth of yen.The Reuters photograph, taken during an on-the-record portion of the meeting, showed Bessent's notepad carrying the underlined heading "To Do" and a single entry reading: "Buy Japanese Yen (JPY) $5-10 bil." The image was taken at 11:33 ET (1533 GMT), with Bessent's name card visible on the conference table directly above the notepad.The image followed come after reports that the US treasury had informed several banks it could intervene in the yen market on Friday and that they should "stand ready for future action."Japanese authorities had already stepped in to support yen earlier, intervening in Tokyo and driving a sharp rise in the currency during morning trading. The yen strengthened further later in the day, with LSEG data showing the dollar slipping from around 158.9 yen at 4:14 p.m. EDT (2014 GMT) to roughly 157.6 yen just before 5 pm EDT (2100 GMT), a fall of about 0.8%.The Financial Times also reported that the US had intervened alongside Tokyo to support the yen, describing it as Washington's first intervention in support of Japan's currency in more than a decade.According to the report, the Federal Reserve Bank of New York sold euros to purchase yen on behalf of the treasury through Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley. Citing people familiar with the matter, the newspaper said it did not identify the amount of yen that was bought.If confirmed, the reported operation would mark the first time since 2011 that the US treasury directly supported the yen. That year, it joined other G7 countries in a coordinated market operation following the earthquake and tsunami in Japan.Separate central bank data released on Friday indicated Japan may have sold as much as $58.97 billion to buy yen on Thursday, pointing to repeated efforts to support the currency.Japan's efforts to stem the yen's weakness have gathered pace in recent months, with the currency seeing sharp gains after repeated intervention measures. On Thursday, the yen climbed suddenly against the dollar during New York trading hours after what market sources said was official yen buying, coordinated with intervention by South Korea. The move pulled the currency away from near four-decade lows and delivered its biggest one-day gain against the dollar in almost two years. It followed around $70 billion in interventions carried out in April and May.On July 30, the yen strengthened by more than 3% to 157.8 per dollar, just a week after touching a near 40-year low of 163.99. The rally came after repeated warnings from Japanese authorities that intervention could come without notice, while a market source in South Korea said the country was selling dollars alongside Japan.Earlier, on April 30, the yen had jumped as much as 3% to 155.5 per dollar after weakening to 160.72, its weakest level since July 2024.
Article Summary: Photograph from US President Donald Trump's cabinet meeting at Camp David showed US treasury secretary Scott Bessent weighing purchases of between $5 billion and $10 billion worth of yen. Japanese authorities had already stepped in to support yen earlier, intervening in Tokyo and driving a sharp rise in the currency during morning trading.

Article Title: After surviving Hurricane Irma, this 16-year-old created a programme that teaches students what schools didn't
Article Text:
After Hurricane Irma, Elise Raurell Built a Programme Schools Never Had—and Nearly 500 Students Have Learned From It. (Photo: Official website)

Turning a childhood fear into a classroom lesson



Students teaching students



A project with a larger purpose



Storm Smart resources are available online through the programme's

and

platforms. A CBS News Miami report has also documented Raurell's initiative and its impact, and you can embed that video at the end of the article.

When Hurricane Irma swept through South Florida, Elise Raurell was just a child. The fallen trees, damaged neighbourhoods and uncertainty left a lasting impression on her. Years later, that frightening experience inspired the 16-year-old to solve a problem she believed schools had overlooked.Instead of waiting for someone else to act, the Florida teenager created Storm Smart—a student-led hurricane preparedness programme designed to teach children what to do before, during and after a storm.What began as her Girl Scout Gold Award project has already reached nearly 500 students, with plans to expand to more schools across South Florida.Growing up in one of the most hurricane-prone regions of the United States, Raurell was surprised that students received little formal education on hurricane preparedness.Speaking to CBS News Miami, she said she realised that although hurricanes are a regular part of life in South Florida, schools weren't teaching students how to prepare for them or stay safe during emergencies.That observation became the foundation for Storm Smart.The programme includes classroom presentations, printable learning materials, online resources and social media content that explain how to prepare emergency kits, stay safe during a hurricane and avoid common dangers after a storm, such as flooded roads and downed power lines.One of Storm Smart's most distinctive features is its peer-to-peer model.Rather than relying solely on teachers, students present the material to classmates, helping spread awareness while developing communication and leadership skills.Raurell says one of the most rewarding parts of the initiative has been watching students learn the information and then confidently teach others, creating a ripple effect that extends beyond a single classroom.Her third learning module focuses specifically on what to do while a hurricane is happening and immediately afterwards—knowledge she believes can make a real difference during emergencies.Raurell hopes Storm Smart will continue expanding so that more schools can include hurricane preparedness as part of everyday learning.Her initiative highlights how students can identify gaps in education and create practical solutions that benefit entire communities.What started as one teenager's response to a frightening childhood memory has become a growing movement to help young people face future storms with greater confidence, knowledge and preparedness.
Article Summary: Elise Raurell, 16, created Storm Smart to teach students about hurricane preparedness. The student-led programme has already reached nearly 500 students in South Florida. It includes classroom presentations, printable learning materials, online resources and social media content that explain how to prepare emergency kits.

Article Title: Who is Ruchika Singh? Noida woman in soup over 'abusive' remarks against PM Modi
Article Text:
A Zero FIR has been registered against Noida resident Ruchika Singh

Who is Ruchika Singh?

Poll Vote & Share your view Are you in favor of stricter laws regarding public speech aimed at political figures? Yes, to maintain respect No, it limits free speech 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





NEW DELHI: A Zero FIR has been registered against Noida resident Ruchika Singh for allegedly using abusive language against Prime Minister Narendra Modi during a protest at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi on July 23.The FIR was lodged at the Expressway police station in Noida on the complaint of a Ghaziabad resident. Police said the case has been registered under Sections 352 (intentional insult to provoke breach of peace), 353(1) (statements conducing to public mischief) and 356(1) (defamation) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).Also read: 'Raised with core values': Lawyer who filed complaint against Noida woman over 'abusive' remarks against PM As the alleged incident took place in Delhi, the Zero FIR will be transferred to the Delhi Police for further investigation.According to information gathered from her social media accounts and conversations with people familiar with her, Ruchika Singh works at a salon and owns a house in Noida. Police said she is a resident of Sector 168 in the city.She came under the spotlight after a video from the Jantar Mantar protest surfaced online, leading to allegations that she used "abusive and objectionable" language against the prime minister. The complainant alleged that her remarks hurt the dignity of the constitutional office and were intended to spread hatred and disturb public peace.A Zero FIR allows a complaint to be registered at any police station regardless of where the alleged offence took place. It is subsequently transferred to the police station with jurisdiction over the case.
Article Summary: A Zero FIR has been registered against Noida resident Ruchika Singh. She is accused of using abusive language against Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The alleged incident took place at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi on July 23. The case will be transferred to the Delhi Police for further investigation.
